correctness.rationale: The Heawood graph is the incidence graph of nonzero F_2^3 point/line labels with zero dot product, 21 edges, automorphism group GL3(F2) extended by polarity of order 336. Perfect-matchable edge subsets form 2201 faces from 24 perfect matchings; ordinary matching complex has 3461 faces. Inspected exhaustive pivot-toggle acyclic discrete Morse checker: full directed Hasse graph 8736/14574 incidences and critical cell pattern one zero-cell plus 16 cells of degree 2/4. Independently recomputed all 24 matchings, the face counts and signed Lefschetz traces for every one of 336 group elements, exactly eight rows; on bipartition-preserving elements both traces agree, on side-exchange elements traces differ by sign, including polarity (-4,4). Since both homologies sit in even degree and are 16-dimensional, exact character equality and Maschke imply the rational sign-twist module isomorphism, not an integral lattice or homotopy equivalence.

evidence: The ordinary module decomposition and both nonequivariant homotopy types do not imply an equivariant sign twist on the other complex without the new G-character computation.
